newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen shares end sharply down on weak sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen shares end sharply down on weak sentiment.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index ended down 5.42 percent on Thursday on institutional profit-taking after Wednesday's surge and the A share index plunged 8.7 percent on weak market sentiment, traders said.
The B index lost 7.26 points to 126.54 on volume of 101.1 million shares at value of HK$472.6 million.
The A index plunged 34.08 points to 357.85 on volume of 576.6 million shares worth 7.3 billion yuan.
Traders said institutions sold heavily in profit-taking on the B share market with investors still jittery over Beijing's crackdown on the stock markets, brokers said.
"Investors offset their positions whenever prices rose because they have little confidence in the market's short-term outlook after the falls earlier this week," an analyst said.
Many B shares closed limit-down today with Dadonghai falling HK$0.36 to HK$3.20 on volume of 5.84 million shares on institutional selling, brokers said.
Changan Automobile traded the most on volume of 11.86 million shares and lost HK$0.20 to HK$3.55.

The A market plummeted with the majority of A shares closing limit-down due to heavy selling in "rubbish stocks" -- shares of smaller firms with poor business results over the past few years, brokers said.
Shenzhen's A share market leader Shenzhen Development Bank fell 0.29 yuan to 16.40 yuan on the session's most active trade of 57.29 million shares.
"A growing number of investors want to leave the A and B markets, at least for a while," a trader said.
The A shares could fall more sharply than B shares because they have registered much stronger gains in the bull run of the past few months, he added.
But several counters with strong earnings records were seen being supported by institutional demand today, brokers said.

Guangdong Power's A shares rose 0.93 yuan or 5.72 percent to 13.49 yuan, with its B shares up HK$0.35 or 6.36 percent to HK$5.85 per share, making them the best performers on the city's A and B share markets on Thursday.
